How to read this comparison

  • Balanced accuracy averages the violation catch rate and compliant-content allow rate. It gives both classes equal weight. It does not make the costs of the two mistakes equal.
  • False-block rate counts false blocks among compliant examples. Catch rate counts correctly blocked examples among actual violations. The error counts and denominators appear in each row’s detail.
  • Macro-F1 averages class-specific F1 scores. MCC summarizes agreement using correct and incorrect decisions in both classes; it is omitted for configurations with unresolved outputs. Neither metric replaces the two error rates.
  • The same validation set selects all configurations within a benchmark: 512 WildGuardTrain examples or 1,920 HateXplain validation examples. These examples had already supported policy authoring. Existing calibrators and ensembles were fitted on separate data; their weights were reused unchanged.
  • “Best” is bounded by the archive. Only candidates with matching full validation and test outputs are eligible. Test-only format ablations and repeatability runs cannot win by test performance. Policies with no saved test run are also absent.
  • Operating targets can fail on test. A 5% false-block limit or 90% catch target was imposed on validation. The table explicitly reports test attainment. These illustrative requirements are not universal safety standards.
  • Confidence intervals use 2,000 shared resamples of duplicate groups. They do not include policy-search uncertainty, upstream benchmark exposure, inference variability, or correction for trying many comparisons.
  • Scope: binary text classification. These experiments do not test a human-review route, image moderation, enterprise permissions, or production prevalence. Cost and latency were not measured under matched serving conditions.

No new API calls, GPU rentals, or model fitting were used to build this leaderboard. Original experiment archives remain unchanged. Created from Harsh Singhal’s Safeguard Eval research.
